title: What to Say in Your Email to a Professor and How to Write It
excerpt: Keep it straight to the point, attach your CV as a PDF, never put links in the email body, and explain the value you bring. Here's how to write it.

blocks.text: But the last point is what we should say in our email and how to write it. This is very important for us and has very very much importance.

My first recommendation is that you state your request completely straight to the point. Meaning when the professor is reading that email, they should understand exactly what your request is. You want PhD admission, you want to get papers, you're inviting the professor to a joint paper, you're looking for a research topic, you're looking for a work project, or any other example. What are you looking for? Write this completely and precisely.
Always remember to introduce yourself very briefly, at the level of one line, at the level of one and a half lines. Introduce yourself so that the professor knows who they're talking to.
Always remember to include an attachment file and put your CV inside it. Meaning send the PDF file of your CV to the professor.
Never Put Links in the Email Body

A very important point is that you should never, never, never put a direct link in the email body. Because many systems that these professor emails run on identify emails that have links inside as spam and filter them, and that professor will never see your email. So as much as possible your email text should be raw text, with no links inside it, and just send an attachment of your own CV.
Use a Formal Template, But Refine It Yourself

What you say and what you don't say naturally you should use that formal template you should have for emails. Now where do you get this template? It's very simple. AI helps you write a good email. But the point is that you should try to refine the email yourself and not leave the whole job to AI. Many professors have a guard against an email being completely written by artificial intelligence. Of course in my opinion it really isn't a problem and it's very good too. But well, some people have a guard against this. So try to not leave your whole job to it either and rewrite that email in your own language. This is very good.
Mention Their Work and Show Your Value

The point is, if you want to invite a professor to a scientific work, you want to get PhD admission, from someone, now any other scientific topic, it's good to study the work that professor has done in that field, at least a little, and make a reference to that work.

For example, I want to now get a PhD from a professor who I know works in my field and the field I'm interested in. Naturally I've taken a look at that professor's papers, I have a view, I bring those papers to hand, I say sir, for example I really liked such and such work, such and such idea of yours, I also work in this field, I have these ideas and also for example I'd like us to work on such and such research question together.

And many times professors also like to see in the email what value you want to add to that research or to that research lab. Meaning in your email you should explain what value and what worth you're bringing to that group, to that research or to that research lab. And definitely express this in your own language.
There's no other special point and these are the most important things you should write.
